findings.evidence: Activation checklist, no explanation needed: native props via `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>`, variants as a discriminated union, `children: ReactNode`, an explicit state type when the initializer is `null`, `[]` or one member of a literal union.
findings.fix: Keep only the item models often get wrong (an explicit useState type when the initializer is null, [] or one literal-union member) and delete the rest. Current models already write ComponentPropsWithoutRef, discriminated variant unions and children: ReactNode without prompting.

findings.fix: Make the migration path its own checklist with an exit checkpoint, for example: '- [ ] tree clean - [ ] deps bumped together - [ ] type codemods run - [ ] diff reviewed - [ ] continue at step 2 to classify and load references'. Right now the migration procedure sits inside the version-pinning step and never says to come back to classification.

findings.fix: Add a row to the SKILL.md load table instead, for example: 'Server Components plus browser storage in a client child: examples/server-components.md and references/hooks.md'. Then every reference loads one level deep from SKILL.md and no example file chains to another reference.

findings.evidence: 11 evals cover refs, forms, generics, routers, SSR storage, optimistic and IME, but none covers the step-1 codemod migration path or Next.js 15 Promise params / use() in a client component
findings.fix: Add an eval that gives a React 18 package.json plus a component using useRef<number>() and an implicit-return ref callback, with this prompt: 'upgrade this to React 19'. Assert that it bumps react, react-dom, @types/react and @types/react-dom together, runs types-react-codemod preset-19 plus the two opt-in transforms, and runs the typecheck. Add a second eval for Next.js 15 page params typed as a Promise.

findings.evidence: 3. Review `git diff`, then typecheck (step 5). If the tree was dirty before step 2, ask the user to commit or stash first, or run the codemods on a new branch
findings.fix: I followed the migration branch, and the dirty-tree check comes after step 1 has already bumped dependencies and step 2 has already run the codemods, so the check comes too late. Move it to a step 0: 'Run git status; if the tree is dirty, ask the user to commit or stash, or create a branch, before any change.' Also add the runtime codemod (`npx codemod@latest react/19/migration-recipe`) before the type codemods. The type codemods alone do not handle removed runtime APIs such as ReactDOM.render or string refs.
